title: You expected God to discard him.
paragraphs: You expected God to discard him.

After the compromise.
After the lust.
After the lies.
After the secret he never should have spoken.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Not because Samson was faithful—
but because God is.
You already know his story… but not like this.

Set apart from birth (Judges 13), marked by a Nazarite vow—
no razor, no wine, no defilement.
Chosen before he ever chose God.

He chased what God warned against.
He touched what God forbade.
He entertained what God said would destroy him.
“Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes.”

You don’t fall into sin overnight.
You slowly replace God’s authority with your own desires.

Defeating enemies.
Tearing lions apart.
Breaking ropes like thread.
It was mercy on borrowed time.

Not just a woman—
a mirror of everything Samson refused to surrender.
“She pressed him hard with her words day after day… and his soul was vexed to death.”

Sin doesn’t always attack.
Sometimes it whispers until you’re tired enough to give in.
The thing that made him different.
And just like that… it was gone.
“But he did not know that the Lord had left him.”

He got up like before…
expected the same power…
but God was no longer with him.

You can keep moving…
talking…
living…
…and not even realize God’s presence has lifted.

Eyes gouged out.
Grinding like an animal.
Mocked by enemies.
But here’s the moment everything turns.

No stage.
No audience.
No strength left to prove anything.
Just a broken man finally turning back.
“O Lord God, please remember me and please strengthen me only this once…”

Not because Samson deserved it—
but because God’s purpose was never dependent on Samson’s perfection.
He did more in his death… than in his life.
So why did God still use Samson?

God’s grace is greater than your failure—
but it will take you through breaking before it restores you.
You see yourself in him, don’t you?

Called… but careless.
Convicted… but still compromising.
Strong on the outside… weak in secret.
Here’s the truth you can’t ignore:
Samson’s story isn’t permission to keep sinning.

It’s a warning of how far you can fall—
and a revelation of how far God’s mercy can reach.
Samson only turned back when everything was gone.
You don’t have to wait for blindness to seek God.
The Gospel is better than Samson’s ending.
Because Jesus didn’t just give one last act of strength.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
While you were still in it.
Will you keep playing with what’s destroying you?
Or will you surrender before it costs you everything?
Because God can still use you…
But He refuses to share you with sin.
